# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit structure and safety-centered identity make enterprise adoption a credibility exercise as much as a technical one. External delivery capacity must extend Claude’s reach without creating inconsistent
expectations around reliability, security, or appropriate use.

The central tension is scale versus coherence. A growing ecosystem can increase market access and implementation capacity, but every partner-introduced variation can create risk if technical guidance, governance, and customer outcomes
diverge from the platform’s intended operating model.

This role appears positioned at the translation boundary between a fast-moving AI platform and organizations that need repeatable ways to introduce it into complex customer environments. Success likely depends on making sound
deployment judgment portable without turning Anthropic into a bespoke-services business.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier-AI public benefit corporation built around Claude and a stated commitment to dependable, understandable, and controllable AI systems. Its market identity combines model research with practical products for
knowledge work, coding, analysis, and business problem solving.

The operating model is product-led, with core platform decisions concentrated inside Anthropic and enterprise reach expanded through external ecosystems. Cloud providers, technology companies, and services firms can broaden access,
but the underlying product, safety posture, and experience standards remain centrally defined.

That model makes ecosystem quality strategically important. Partners are not merely routes to market; they influence how customers evaluate the platform’s usefulness, implementation maturity, and trustworthiness. Inconsistent
delivery can become both a commercial and brand risk.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco, Anthropic has framed its purpose around advancing AI that is useful while remaining aligned with human interests. This framing places operational weight on how enterprise use
cases are selected, implemented, monitored, and communicated.

Claude spans both end-user and developer-oriented contexts. That breadth introduces architectural complexity: customer value may involve individual productivity, internal workflow redesign, embedded applications, data-connected
experiences, or software development. Each context has different ownership, risk, and change-management requirements.

A likely operating pressure sits between centrally managed platform priorities and local market realities encountered by external delivery organizations. The highest-value contribution is likely not unlimited customization, but a
disciplined mechanism that distinguishes reusable market learning from account-specific requests.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic was founded by Daniela Amodei and Dario Amodei, whose leadership context reinforces the company’s safety-oriented public identity and public-benefit framing.

Likely stakeholder relationships center on:
- Partnerships leaders, who determine ecosystem focus, coverage, and strategic investment.

The stakeholder challenge is reconciling commercial urgency with platform discipline. Strong leadership in this setting creates common language for customer outcomes, technical constraints, partner readiness, and escalation paths.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as an AI assistant designed to be safe, accurate, and secure. Its broader corporate positioning emphasizes reliability, interpretability, and steerability. These signals suggest that production
architecture discussions should begin with controls and operational accountability rather than generic experimentation.

Claude’s use across complex analysis, software tasks, and problem solving means customer deployments may vary considerably in data sensitivity, integration depth, end-user interaction, and business criticality. A credible ecosystem
needs clear ways to distinguish low-risk exploration from durable operational use.

The most useful architecture assets are likely practical decision frameworks: where model behavior ends and application logic begins; how customer data is governed; when human review is needed; who owns monitoring; and how recurring
implementation findings become platform learning.

A partner-facing technical function can strengthen adoption by making these decisions understandable and repeatable. Its value is not simply explaining product features, but helping external organizations apply consistent judgment in
real customer situations.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a partner network across cloud, technology, and services categories. That indicates an ecosystem model in which multiple partner types contribute different parts of enterprise adoption, rather than
operating as isolated channels.

Cloud partners shape procurement paths, infrastructure preferences, and enterprise confidence. Technology partners affect integration opportunities and workflow fit. Services organizations influence implementation execution,
organizational change, and the quality of customer-facing technical guidance.

The coordination challenge is that these groups are interdependent. A customer outcome may require cloud alignment, product integration, delivery capability, and clear governance guidance at the same time. Fragmented technical
messaging across those parties can slow adoption or weaken trust.

The highest-leverage ecosystem approach is likely based on repeatable outcomes: well-bounded use cases, clear readiness indicators, validated implementation patterns, shared vocabulary, and an orderly path for escalating field
insights. This creates partner autonomy while preserving product coherence.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public posture combines frontier-model research, a safety-centered identity, Claude’s expanding practical use, and a visible partner ecosystem. Together, these signals point to a company facing the challenge of turning
strong platform demand into dependable adoption across many external delivery paths.

The urgency is less about adding partner logos than making partner-supported customer experiences consistently credible. As adoption expands across knowledge-work and developer contexts, uneven implementation patterns can produce
commercial drag, avoidable support burden, and confusion about responsible operating practices.

A mature partner architecture capability can help Anthropic scale without sacrificing the qualities that distinguish its market position. It can turn recurring field questions into reusable guidance and ensure that ecosystem growth
improves, rather than dilutes, customer confidence.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Scaling enterprise AI adoption through partner-ready technical operating models.
- Creating reusable architecture guidance for varied customer environments.
- Connecting cloud, technology, and services ecosystems around shared customer outcomes.
- Establishing technical quality bars that preserve trust during rapid growth.
- Turning recurring field observations into structured product and engineering inputs.
- Balancing commercial momentum with security, reliability, and accountable use.
- Enabling industry adaptation without creating uncontrolled customization.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s public-benefit identity makes deployment quality part of the company’s commercial differentiation.

Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit structure and safety-centered identity make enterprise adoption a credibility exercise as much as a technical one. External delivery capacity must extend Claude’s reach without creating inconsistent
expectations around reliability, security, or appropriate use.

The central tension is scale versus coherence. A growing ecosystem can increase market access and implementation capacity, but every partner-introduced variation can create risk if technical guidance, governance, and customer outcomes
diverge from the platform’s intended operating model.

This role appears positioned at the translation boundary between a fast-moving AI platform and organizations that need repeatable ways to introduce it into complex customer environments. Success likely depends on making sound
deployment judgment portable without turning Anthropic into a bespoke-services business.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier-AI public benefit corporation built around Claude and a stated commitment to dependable, understandable, and controllable AI systems. Its market identity combines model research with practical products for
knowledge work, coding, analysis, and business problem solving.

The operating model is product-led, with core platform decisions concentrated inside Anthropic and enterprise reach expanded through external ecosystems. Cloud providers, technology companies, and services firms can broaden access,
but the underlying product, safety posture, and experience standards remain centrally defined.

That model makes ecosystem quality strategically important. Partners are not merely routes to market; they influence how customers evaluate the platform’s usefulness, implementation maturity, and trustworthiness. Inconsistent
delivery can become both a commercial and brand risk.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco, Anthropic has framed its purpose around advancing AI that is useful while remaining aligned with human interests. This framing places operational weight on how enterprise use
cases are selected, implemented, monitored, and communicated.

Claude spans both end-user and developer-oriented contexts. That breadth introduces architectural complexity: customer value may involve individual productivity, internal workflow redesign, embedded applications, data-connected
experiences, or software development. Each context has different ownership, risk, and change-management requirements.

A likely operating pressure sits between centrally managed platform priorities and local market realities encountered by external delivery organizations. The highest-value contribution is likely not unlimited customization, but a
disciplined mechanism that distinguishes reusable market learning from account-specific requests.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic was founded by Daniela Amodei and Dario Amodei, whose leadership context reinforces the company’s safety-oriented public identity and public-benefit framing.

Likely stakeholder relationships center on:
- Partnerships leaders, who determine ecosystem focus, coverage, and strategic investment.

The stakeholder challenge is reconciling commercial urgency with platform discipline. Strong leadership in this setting creates common language for customer outcomes, technical constraints, partner readiness, and escalation paths.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as an AI assistant designed to be safe, accurate, and secure. Its broader corporate positioning emphasizes reliability, interpretability, and steerability. These signals suggest that production
architecture discussions should begin with controls and operational accountability rather than generic experimentation.

Claude’s use across complex analysis, software tasks, and problem solving means customer deployments may vary considerably in data sensitivity, integration depth, end-user interaction, and business criticality. A credible ecosystem
needs clear ways to distinguish low-risk exploration from durable operational use.

The most useful architecture assets are likely practical decision frameworks: where model behavior ends and application logic begins; how customer data is governed; when human review is needed; who owns monitoring; and how recurring
implementation findings become platform learning.

A partner-facing technical function can strengthen adoption by making these decisions understandable and repeatable. Its value is not simply explaining product features, but helping external organizations apply consistent judgment in
real customer situations.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a partner network across cloud, technology, and services categories. That indicates an ecosystem model in which multiple partner types contribute different parts of enterprise adoption, rather than
operating as isolated channels.

Cloud partners shape procurement paths, infrastructure preferences, and enterprise confidence. Technology partners affect integration opportunities and workflow fit. Services organizations influence implementation execution,
organizational change, and the quality of customer-facing technical guidance.

The coordination challenge is that these groups are interdependent. A customer outcome may require cloud alignment, product integration, delivery capability, and clear governance guidance at the same time. Fragmented technical
messaging across those parties can slow adoption or weaken trust.

The highest-leverage ecosystem approach is likely based on repeatable outcomes: well-bounded use cases, clear readiness indicators, validated implementation patterns, shared vocabulary, and an orderly path for escalating field
insights. This creates partner autonomy while preserving product coherence.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public posture combines frontier-model research, a safety-centered identity, Claude’s expanding practical use, and a visible partner ecosystem. Together, these signals point to a company facing the challenge of turning
strong platform demand into dependable adoption across many external delivery paths.

The urgency is less about adding partner logos than making partner-supported customer experiences consistently credible. As adoption expands across knowledge-work and developer contexts, uneven implementation patterns can produce
commercial drag, avoidable support burden, and confusion about responsible operating practices.

A mature partner architecture capability can help Anthropic scale without sacrificing the qualities that distinguish its market position. It can turn recurring field questions into reusable guidance and ensure that ecosystem growth
improves, rather than dilutes, customer confidence.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Scaling enterprise AI adoption through partner-ready technical operating models.
- Creating reusable architecture guidance for varied customer environments.
- Connecting cloud, technology, and services ecosystems around shared customer outcomes.
- Establishing technical quality bars that preserve trust during rapid growth.
- Turning recurring field observations into structured product and engineering inputs.
- Balancing commercial momentum with security, reliability, and accountable use.
- Enabling industry adaptation without creating uncontrolled customization.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s public-benefit identity makes deployment quality part of the company’s commercial differentiation.

| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit structure and safety-centered identity make enterprise adoption a credibility exercise as much as a technical one. External delivery capacity must extend Claude’s reach without creating inconsistent
expectations around reliability, security, or appropriate use.

The central tension is scale versus coherence. A growing ecosystem can increase market access and implementation capacity, but every partner-introduced variation can create risk if technical guidance, governance, and customer outcomes
diverge from the platform’s intended operating model.

This role appears positioned at the translation boundary between a fast-moving AI platform and organizations that need repeatable ways to introduce it into complex customer environments. Success likely depends on making sound
deployment judgment portable without turning Anthropic into a bespoke-services business.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier-AI public benefit corporation built around Claude and a stated commitment to dependable, understandable, and controllable AI systems. Its market identity combines model research with practical products for
knowledge work, coding, analysis, and business problem solving.

The operating model is product-led, with core platform decisions concentrated inside Anthropic and enterprise reach expanded through external ecosystems. Cloud providers, technology companies, and services firms can broaden access,
but the underlying product, safety posture, and experience standards remain centrally defined.

That model makes ecosystem quality strategically important. Partners are not merely routes to market; they influence how customers evaluate the platform’s usefulness, implementation maturity, and trustworthiness. Inconsistent
delivery can become both a commercial and brand risk.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco, Anthropic has framed its purpose around advancing AI that is useful while remaining aligned with human interests. This framing places operational weight on how enterprise use
cases are selected, implemented, monitored, and communicated.

Claude spans both end-user and developer-oriented contexts. That breadth introduces architectural complexity: customer value may involve individual productivity, internal workflow redesign, embedded applications, data-connected
experiences, or software development. Each context has different ownership, risk, and change-management requirements.

A likely operating pressure sits between centrally managed platform priorities and local market realities encountered by external delivery organizations. The highest-value contribution is likely not unlimited customization, but a
disciplined mechanism that distinguishes reusable market learning from account-specific requests.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic was founded by Daniela Amodei and Dario Amodei, whose leadership context reinforces the company’s safety-oriented public identity and public-benefit framing.

Likely stakeholder relationships center on:
- Partnerships leaders, who determine ecosystem focus, coverage, and strategic investment.

The stakeholder challenge is reconciling commercial urgency with platform discipline. Strong leadership in this setting creates common language for customer outcomes, technical constraints, partner readiness, and escalation paths.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as an AI assistant designed to be safe, accurate, and secure. Its broader corporate positioning emphasizes reliability, interpretability, and steerability. These signals suggest that production
architecture discussions should begin with controls and operational accountability rather than generic experimentation.

Claude’s use across complex analysis, software tasks, and problem solving means customer deployments may vary considerably in data sensitivity, integration depth, end-user interaction, and business criticality. A credible ecosystem
needs clear ways to distinguish low-risk exploration from durable operational use.

The most useful architecture assets are likely practical decision frameworks: where model behavior ends and application logic begins; how customer data is governed; when human review is needed; who owns monitoring; and how recurring
implementation findings become platform learning.

A partner-facing technical function can strengthen adoption by making these decisions understandable and repeatable. Its value is not simply explaining product features, but helping external organizations apply consistent judgment in
real customer situations.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a partner network across cloud, technology, and services categories. That indicates an ecosystem model in which multiple partner types contribute different parts of enterprise adoption, rather than
operating as isolated channels.

Cloud partners shape procurement paths, infrastructure preferences, and enterprise confidence. Technology partners affect integration opportunities and workflow fit. Services organizations influence implementation execution,
organizational change, and the quality of customer-facing technical guidance.

The coordination challenge is that these groups are interdependent. A customer outcome may require cloud alignment, product integration, delivery capability, and clear governance guidance at the same time. Fragmented technical
messaging across those parties can slow adoption or weaken trust.

The highest-leverage ecosystem approach is likely based on repeatable outcomes: well-bounded use cases, clear readiness indicators, validated implementation patterns, shared vocabulary, and an orderly path for escalating field
insights. This creates partner autonomy while preserving product coherence.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public posture combines frontier-model research, a safety-centered identity, Claude’s expanding practical use, and a visible partner ecosystem. Together, these signals point to a company facing the challenge of turning
strong platform demand into dependable adoption across many external delivery paths.

The urgency is less about adding partner logos than making partner-supported customer experiences consistently credible. As adoption expands across knowledge-work and developer contexts, uneven implementation patterns can produce
commercial drag, avoidable support burden, and confusion about responsible operating practices.

A mature partner architecture capability can help Anthropic scale without sacrificing the qualities that distinguish its market position. It can turn recurring field questions into reusable guidance and ensure that ecosystem growth
improves, rather than dilutes, customer confidence.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Scaling enterprise AI adoption through partner-ready technical operating models.
- Creating reusable architecture guidance for varied customer environments.
- Connecting cloud, technology, and services ecosystems around shared customer outcomes.
- Establishing technical quality bars that preserve trust during rapid growth.
- Turning recurring field observations into structured product and engineering inputs.
- Balancing commercial momentum with security, reliability, and accountable use.
- Enabling industry adaptation without creating uncontrolled customization.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s public-benefit identity makes deployment quality part of the company’s commercial differentiation.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The job description and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

  "jd_text": "Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}
